title: Why your Pods magically restart when they crash
caption: ReplicaSets keep your Pods alive automatically. Have you ever written one directly?

scenes.vo: If your Pod dies at midnight, who replaces it? Meet the ReplicaSet, the silent engine that keeps identical copies running without downtime.
scenes.heading: REPLICASET

scenes.vo: Think of it like a bouncer with a strict headcount clicker. You demand three Pods, so it guarantees exactly three.
scenes.heading: THE BOUNCER
scenes.line: A bouncer enforcing an exact headcount

scenes.vo: When a Pod crashes, the active count drops. The controller notices right away and spins up a brand-new replacement.
scenes.heading: SELF HEALING

scenes.vo: The golden rule? You almost never write a ReplicaSet directly. You write a Deployment instead, which manages ReplicaSets for seamless rollouts.
scenes.heading: THE TRICK

scenes.vo: ReplicaSets guarantee target headcounts, rapid recovery, and effortless scaling. Follow along for more Kubernetes explained in plain English.
scenes.heading: REPLICASET
